purpose:
To provide grant funding of £100,000
towards expanding the scope of the South East Rivers Trust’s
project to restore Petty’s Brook in Chineham, in support of
the borough council’s Ecological Emergency and Declaration on
Rights of Rivers.
content:
To provide grant funding of £100,000
towards expanding the scope of the South East Rivers Trust’s
project to restore Petty’s Brook in Chineham, in support of
the borough council’s Ecological Emergency and Declaration on
Rights of Rivers.

The decision is:
 

·      
To provide grant funding of £100,000 towards expanding the
scope of the South East Rivers Trust’s project to restore
Petty’s Brook in Chineham, in support of the borough
council’s Ecological Emergency and Declaration on Rights of
Rivers.

The proposal to provide
£100k of grant funding to SERT to support and extend the
scope of the Petty’s Brook improvement project will provide
significant benefits in support of a range of objectives set out in
adopted strategies.  Doing so recognises
the importance attached to the natural environment by the Borough
Council. 
 


Whilst it is recommended that a
grant of £100,000 is provided, there remains the option
of:

·      
Not providing a grant;
or

·      
Providing a sum less than or
greater than £100,000.
Noting the Rivers Trust is in
receipt of funding associated with Thames Water, additional funding
by the Borough Council will ensure that the scope can be widened to
provide additional benefits.  Without
additional funding or providing a lesser amount, the project can
only be delivered across a smaller area and recognising the impact
of inflation and increases in costs, there is concern that without
additional funding, the project may be reduced in scale and
ambition.  There are economies of scale
in extending the scope of the project as outlined in this report,
given the resources required to plan for an oversee implementation
that which has already secured funding.
Equally, there is scope to
provide additional funding to support wider benefits.  However, this needs to be balanced against the
money held by the Borough Council in the Climate Change Reserve and
the need to use this in the most effective manner possible to
support wider objectives in response to the Climate
Emergency.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to provide £100,000 grant funding to support the restoration of Petty's Brook in Chineham.

action plan are public facing, this could undermine confidence in
the council’s ability to deliver under its Biodiversity Duty.
Not updating the action plan will hamper the adaptability and
efficient monitoring and delivery of the council’s work under
the Strategy. This option is therefore rejected.

purpose:
To dispose of Vyne Meadow car park as it is
surplus to operational requirements to enable the delivery of
affordable housing
content:
To dispose of Vyne Meadow car park as it is
surplus to operational requirements to enable the delivery of
affordable housing

Cabinet agree:
 
1.     
In principle to support the disposal via a conditional land sale of
Vyne Meadow car park to a Preferred Partner Registered Provider
(RP) for less than best consideration, upon the basis the disposal
is likely to contribute to the improvement of the economic, social
and environmental wellbeing of the area and its residents, pursuant
to S123 Local Government Act 1972 to enable the delivery of
affordable housing on the basis that the car park is surplus to the
Council’s operational requirements.

 
2.     
A disposal is subject to:
 

·      
A satisfactory scheme;

·      
Agreement of Heads of Terms;

·      
Agreement of a satisfactory scheme and a s123 valuation report;

·      
The grant of Planning Permission for the development of Vyne Meadow
car park for Affordable Housing;

·      
Proof of funding for delivery;

·      
Inclusion of an option for the council to repurchase the Vyne
Meadow car park at the disposal price from the successful RP if the
Planning Permission is not implemented within or development is not
completed within a defined period;

·      
Notification of any subsidy under the Subsidy Control Act.
 
3.     
That authority be delegated to the Director of Regeneration, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Resident Services and
Housing and Cabinet Member for Finance and Property, to finalise
heads of terms for the disposal of the site to a RP and to enter
into a contract for sale and conclude the transaction.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to dispose of Vyne Meadow car park to facilitate the construction of affordable housing.

purpose:
To consider a Neighbourhood Planning Grant
application from Highclere Parish Council.
content:
To consider a Neighbourhood Planning Grant
application from Highclere Parish Council.

To award Highclere Parish Council £8,890
under the Neighbourhood Planning Grant Scheme to progress the
Highclere Neighbourhood Plan through to adoption, and to draw up to
this amount from the Neighbourhood Planning Reserve in line with
the payment timings specified in the Legal Agreement.

The Highclere Neighbourhood Plan (NP) has been
under preparation since 2018.The designation of the area for the
purposes of neighbourhood planning was made in November 2018, and
in October 2024 the council undertook a screening for Strategic
Environmental Assessment (SEA) and Habitats Regulations Assessment
(HRA). It is considered that the plan is significantly progressed,
and grant funding would assist the parish council to complete the
project.
 
Highclere Parish Council’s grant
application is supplemented by a quote prepared by planning
consultancy PlanET setting out a range
of tasks required to take the NP through to adoption. Whilst the
Parish Council is eligible to receive up to£10,000, as it
meets the relevant eligibility criteria of allocating sites to meet
its housing need in full, following an assessment of spend
proposals against each of the more detailed eligibility criteria, a
reduced amount is supported. The list of costs which can be covered
by the grant is set out in the eligibility criteria on the NP grant
scheme webpage.

The council could decide not to award the
grant or award a different value.

None
topline: The Chief Finance Officer has decided to award Highclere Parish Council a grant to progress the Highclere Neighbourhood Plan.

and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Boardor Whitchurch Town

content:
This report seeks authority for the
council to accept a transfer of the Health Care Facility Land as
defined in the planning obligation to be made in connection with
application 22/03219/FUL to allow development of a health care
facility in the future to be affected either by the North Hampshire
and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Boardor Whitchurch Town
Council.
 

The decision is that:
 

·      
The Council agrees to accept the offer of a transfer of the Health
Care Facility Land defined in a planning obligation to be made
pursuant to planning application 22/03219/FUL.

·      
Power be delegated to the Director of Regeneration to take all
steps necessary in connection with the transfer of the Health Care
Facility Land to the Council including a subsequent transfer to
either the North Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care
Board  the Town Council or any successor
body to give effect to the said planning obligation

Authority is sought for the council to accept
a transfer of the Health Care Facility Land and hold it for
planning purposes for a period of 10 years so that the health care
provider can facilitate the development of a health care facility
on the land. The land will be transferred either to the North
Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board or the Town
Council.  If it is to be transferred to
any other person or body further consent will be needed from the
Developer.

Neither the North Hampshire and Isle of Wight
Integrated Care Board nor Whitchurch Town Council are currently
able to enter into the planning
obligation and give covenants to use the Health Facility Land for
expansion of health care facilities within Whitchurch.  If the Council does not accept a transfer of the
Health Care Facility Land then the land
will not be secured for future use for health care within
Whitchurch.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to accept a transfer of Health Care Facility Land for future development of a health care facility in Whitchurch.

Strategic Partner Contributions were

content:
Strategic Partner Contributions were
introduced in 2023 following a review of the way in which the
council funds community and voluntary sector organisations. They
provide revenue core funding to support organisations providing
specialist services that are integral to delivering and supporting
Council Plan priorities. This report provides a summary of the
process followed to review current Strategic Partner Contributions
and seeks approval for the recommendations for funding allocations
for individual organisations to start in April 2026.

The
decision is:
 
Note the process undertaken to
review the Strategic Partner Contributions for the community and
voluntary sector as outlined in this report.
 
Agree the individual
allocations for 2026 to 2028 as listed in the report, subject to
approval of the proposed budgets by council on 26th February
2026.
 
Delegate authority to the
relevant Head of Service to agree the priority objectives and key
performance indicators (KPIs) for each recipient organisation and
formalise funding agreements.
 
Options considered and rejected:
 
Other options considered were
in relation to the individual allocations. All current recipients
have been subject to an increase in costs and reduction in the
availability of other grants as well as being affected by the
cost-of-living difficulties facing our residents. Reducing the
total budget, or for any individual organisations would lead to a
reduction in the services they could offer residents.
 
Summary and reasons for the decision:
 
This funding supports key
organisations in delivering services and activities in support of
council priorities. Withdrawing or reducing this funding would lead
to a significant reduction in services.

purpose:
To agree the council’s response to HCC to approve the
final draft LNRS.
content:
To agree the council’s response to HCC to approve the
final draft LNRS.

Submit the council’s response to
Hampshire CC to approve the final draft LNRS

The LNRS is one of the four key instruments
from the Environment Act 2021. Led by Hampshire County council as
the responsible authority, Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council
has a statutory role as a supporting authority. This role permits
the council to respond or object to the LNRS at certain stages of
the process, with any such response due within 28 days.

Do not provide delegated authority –The
council’s consultation response, if it chose to provide one,
would need to be approved by the Leader or Cabinet prior to its
submission. This could cause a delay beyond the consultation window
resulting in the required response falling outside of the 28-day
required timeframe and the responsible authority not accepting
it.

None

purpose:
To outline how the

emissions
content:
To outline how the
Council intends to achieve carbon neutrality for its operational
emissions
 

Cabinet:
 
1.     
Note the positive work and progress in reducing emissions, with a
near two-thirds reduction in net emissions by the 24/25 financial
year, compared to the baseline of the 18/19 financial year.

 
2.     
Recognise that there remain emissions that are
‘hard-to-eliminate’ given existing operational
arrangements, such as those associated with the Aquadrome.
 
3.     
Recognise the work under way to provide a replacement pool at the
leisure centre and the associated environmental standard that must
be reached;
 
4.     
That council-owned carbon credits are included in carbon reporting
to make the authority operationally carbon neutral in 2025, subject
to confirmation of its emissions in early summer 2026; and
 
5.     
Purchase no further carbon credits, but continue to support actions
to reduce emissions locally, including through opportunities
presented through improving the natural environment in the
borough.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for achieving carbon neutrality for operational emissions
